tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-27 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view (Integrated and multi-utilities B, Regulated networks C, Renewable generators D). Utilities at industry level were not readable this week (Jefferies' utilities dailies arrived without readable views) and no power-price reading reached the pack, so the condition for B (a second power-price reading with relative strength leaving D) is untested; relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior). Counter-case: Oppenheimer's 2027 theme (Goldman, 22-Nov) is beneficiaries of lower bond yields, which is this industry. Moves to B on a second power-price reading with relative strength leaving D.

sector.why: Overweight, carried; the condition for A (a second power-price reading) is unmet and the condition back to C (Nordic forwards read lower or relative strength F) is untested: no power-price reading reached the pack, relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Goldman's gas forecast (45 euros per megawatt hour in 2027 from 70 to 100; Dart, 22-Nov) is the one new fact and it cuts both ways for generators. Pool names VERBUND (leaving the Pool, week 1 of 2), PGE, Iberdrola, Endesa, Energa, Electrica, Public Power. Counter-case: one house, one deal, and a lower gas price is a lower power price. To A on a second power-price reading; back to C if Nordic forwards are read lower or relative strength falls to F.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the first country-specific evidence since the row was set: Germany's composite PMI is 55.0, a 56-month high (Goldman Economics, 24-Nov; S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov), with automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries; Danske, 26-Nov) and Bunds forecast at 3.1% by end-2027 (Marshall, 22-Nov); the signed Lists statement asks for a country view wherever there is evidence, and this week there is. Eleven Pool stocks are German-listed. Counter-case: one PMI print is one month, the US tariff lands on the EU at 15% inclusive, Stehn's winter energy squeeze applies to the euro area, and the German Pool names (Bayer, Symrise, Evonik, Talanx, Sartorius, Deutsche Borse among them) are global businesses on which a country letter is a blunt instrument. Back to C on a German PMI read under 52 or a second month of euro area services PMIs falling.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
